Bihu Festival Questions with Answers

Bihu is the national festival of Assam and one of the most frequently asked topics in the Art and Culture section. The questions here cover the three Bihus, their timing, the Bihu dance and the folk songs that go with it.

The Three Bihus

Assam celebrates three Bihus in a year. Bohag or Rongali Bihu in April marks the Assamese New Year and the spring season. Kati or Kongali Bihu in October is a quiet festival of the sowing season. Magh or Bhogali Bihu in January celebrates the harvest with feasts.

Bihu Dance and Music

The Bihu dance is performed by young men and women, usually during Rongali Bihu, with the dhol, pepa, taal and gagana. The Bihu geet are folk songs about love, nature and rural life.

Cultural Importance

Bihu reflects the agricultural cycle of Assam and the close bond between the people and nature. Husori, the door-to-door Bihu performance, and the Bihu Sanmilan are part of the tradition.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Bihus are celebrated in Assam?

Assam celebrates three Bihus: Bohag or Rongali Bihu, Kati or Kongali Bihu, and Magh or Bhogali Bihu.

Which Bihu marks the Assamese New Year?

Bohag Bihu, also called Rongali Bihu, is celebrated in mid-April and marks the Assamese New Year.

Which instruments are used in Bihu dance?

The main instruments are the dhol, pepa, taal, gagana and toka, along with the Bihu songs sung by the dancers.
